title: CNN attention placement changes decision-space alignment in benchmark experiments
summary: A decision-space analysis found that the relationship between predicted and observed classification-margin changes depends on where visual-attention modules are placed. The paper evaluates the effect on CIFAR-100 using SimAM and CBAM across five CNN backbones; the finding is bounded to those models and experiments.
ai_technology: Decision Alignment Score analysis with SimAM and CBAM attention modules
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed arXiv metadata

evidence.tested: The study compares attention placements and margin-alignment measures on CIFAR-100 across five CNN backbones, using SimAM and CBAM.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns the studied architectures, attention modules and benchmark; it does not establish effects across other tasks or models.
evidence.ai_role: The paper derives a decision-space measure and evaluates how learned visual attention changes CNN feature perturbations and classification margins.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
